To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HelioFth cloud mask and cloud coverage product has been developed for the Meteosat Second Generation and is based on infrared window observations.
HelioFTH provides a cloud mask with a high detection probability for low and middle level clouds.

the HelioFth CFC is able reproduce the day-to day variability of the surface CFC, that the HelioFT HCC is able to detect cloud-free HCC with a probability comparable to ISCCP and that HelioFT CTP is able to reproduce a CTP that is comparable to ISCC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an operational cloud mask and cloud CFC retrieval scheme that is based on IR-only observations.
the development and evaluation of a self-calibrating, IR-only cloud mask algorithm and a cloud CTP and CFC retrieval scheme for Meteosat IR data.
the retrieval of cloud physical properties from geostationarly satellites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HelioFTH provides an independent and self-calibrating IR-only CTP and CFC retrieval scheme that is applicable to all IR sensors with a window channel.
the HelioFth CFC and HCC retrieval is a promising alternative to ISCCP and CM SAF products.
the HelioFHT CFC is a promising product that can be used to improve the quality of cloud products from other satellite sensors and NWP models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithm is able to reproduce surface CFC and HCC with a high degree of accuracy.
we were able to develop an operational cloud mask and CFC retrieval algorithm for Meteosat-8 and -9, and Metop-A and -B.
the HelioFth scheme can provide cloud physical properties from Meteosat observations in the same way as ISCCP and CM SAF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HelioFth CFC product can be used as a reliable input for the HelioFt algorithm to estimate the surface solar radiation.
the cloud mask and CTP retrieval scheme presented in this study is applicable to the entire Meteosat time period and is not affected by the sensor degradation.
the cloud index concept can be applied to the full temporal resolution of geostationary observations.
